title: Public service operational delivery officer
change: Occupational standard, assessment plan and funding band revised,
overviewOfRole: Operational delivery officers are the face of public sector organisations, working directly with the public or supporting colleagues who do.

knowledges.detail: Communication styles and techniques.
Information presentation techniques.
Techniques to handle challenging conversations.
Principles of escalation and support arrangements in the organisation.
Techniques for stakeholder and relationship management, including the importance of building and maintaining internal and external professional relationships and the impact these can have.
Methods to identify stakeholders and their needs or requirements.
Relevant diversity, equity and inclusion policies within the organisation.
How to role model appropriate behaviours within the workplace and identify and tackle inappropriate language and behaviours.
The Profession's skills framework and its application within their role, and how to use it to support personal development.
Techniques to identify, plan and action personal development, including seeking feedback from colleagues.
The purpose of the organisation, their role within it, and the broader Operational Delivery Profession.
Principles of problem solving, continuous improvement and change methods, models or techniques.
Techniques for gathering, recording, processing and interpreting data.
Data handling statutory and organisational requirements and how to comply with them.
Decision making techniques.
Organisation's decision making processes including relevant legislation to be considered.
Relevant policies, regulations, codes of practice, and legal requirements.
Organisation's environmental and sustainability policies and procedures.
Organisational health, safety and wellbeing requirements and mandatory training for the role.
Organisation's framework, policy, processes for identifying non-compliance or legal offences and appropriate actions.
Working practices and time and task management to meet organisational quality standards or objectives.
The organisation’s service users, their different needs and reasons for interacting with the service.
Principles for service excellence and how to manage differing service user’s needs.
Characteristics and signs of vulnerable service users and the process to provide effective support and assistance.
General administrative activities as required relevant to the role e.g. dealing with correspondence, organising and preparing meetings, task and time management.
Digital applications, tools and systems relevant to role, including the safe use of technology.
The capabilities and benefits, limitations and risks of using AI and digital tools within the role, including organisational policy for appropriate use.

behaviours.detail: Act in a professional manner, with honesty, integrity, objectivity, and impartiality, treating all colleagues, service users and stakeholders fairly and with respect.
Build relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders, supporting an inclusive culture which enables understanding of different perspectives.
Take the initiative and responsibility for own learning and development and listen to and act on feedback from colleagues.
Look for solutions to problems and where necessary refers to others with a focus on bringing about change and improvement.
Work to ensure a safe environment for themselves and others.
Work collaboratively and at pace, manage own time to complete tasks to schedule and display resilience and flexibility when facing change and challenges.

skills.detail: Present information using appropriate communication methods to facilitate understanding and meet the needs of the individual or audience.
Handle challenging conversations, following organisational procedures for escalating complex or difficult issues.
Develop relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders and maintain where necessary.
Support diversity, equity and inclusion in the workplace.
Recognise inappropriate language and behaviours and take appropriate action.
Seek ways to continuously improve, use the Profession's skills framework to identify skills gaps and create a personal development plan.
Act on feedback from colleagues to identify development areas for change.
Identify problems, find potential solutions and refer to others where necessary, with a focus on bringing about change and improvement.
Share knowledge and skills with others to support learning, improved outcomes and readiness for change.
Gather, process and record data safely and securely.
Interpret data to identify gaps or issues with data integrity.
Make timely decisions and recommendations considering all information, organisational processes, relevant legislation and implications of those decisions.
Comply with relevant policies, regulations, codes of practice and legal requirements.
Support sustainable and greener methods of working.
Maintain safety and wellbeing, accessing organisational support mechanisms or signposting to others if required.
Follow organisational processes for identifying and dealing with non-compliance or legal offences.
Deliver services to meet organisational quality standards or targets.
Identify the needs of service users and deal with them or signpost to relevant teams, stakeholders or organisations when required.
Follow organisational procedures to prioritise the welfare of service users and provide further support where necessary.
Carry out administrative duties as required.
Select and appropriately use organisationally relevant digital applications, tools or systems to complete tasks.

clusterDescription: Co-ordination, management and delivery of specific business processes and also their direct provision to users

duties.dutyDetail: Communicate with stakeholders or service users providing accurate information using appropriate channels to resolve queries.
Manage challenging conversations, seeking support and guidance when required.
Develop and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Work as part of a team and act as a role model, promoting an inclusive workforce.
Take ownership of personal development, seeking ways to continuously improve.
Develop solutions to problems with a focus on bringing about change and improvement, refer to others where necessary.
Gather, process and record information and data.
Make timely decisions and support others in decision making, escalating complex or difficult issues where necessary.
Comply with legal requirements and organisational policies, following relevant processes and frameworks.
Take responsibility for own health, safety and wellbeing, be alert to health and safety concerns at work, raising issues or taking appropriate action for self and others.
Identify non-compliance or legal offences and the actions required to respond appropriately.
Perform activities to deliver the service, ensuring work meets quality standards or objectives.
Provide high standards of service delivery  when dealing with service users with differing needs or enquiries.
Carry out tasks and activities to meet organisation’s administrative requirements.
Use digital equipment and resources confidently and effectively to complete tasks, including applications, tools and systems.
